author: Simplilearn
description:
Ever wondered how Netflix, Spotify, or YouTube seem to “know” exactly what you’ll like next? That’s machine learning in action—especially recommendation systems. Instead of guessing, these systems quietly watch what you do: what you click, watch, skip, or replay. Over time, they learn patterns in your behavior and compare them with millions of other users to predict what you’re most likely to enjoy next. It’s like a friend who has watched every movie ever made and remembers everything you’ve liked before. This same idea of learning from data instead of hard-coded rules now powers not just recommendations, but also fraud detection, search ranking, ads, and even self-driving cars. In simple terms: machine learning is when computers learn from experience (data) to make smarter decisions—just like we do, but at massive scale.

author: Simplilearn
description:
If you're looking to enter the world of data science, there are a few key terms you need to understand. 

First, Machine Learning is when computers learn from data instead of being programmed step by step. You provide the data, and the computer finds patterns and improves over time. 

Next, Big Data refers to massive amounts of data that are so large and complex that traditional tools can’t handle them. This includes things like social media posts, online shopping history, and banking records. Artificial Intelligence (AI) involves making machines "smart" and capable of tasks such as face recognition, voice assistants, and self-driving cars.
Finally, Data Analytics is the process of examining data to uncover patterns and inform better decision-making. For example, it helps businesses understand customer behavior and predict future sales.

In summary, Machine Learning helps computers learn, Big Data is about vast amounts of information, AI makes machines smarter, and Data Analytics help
title: Top Data Science Terms You Should Know | Simplify Data Science Concepts #shorts #simplilearn
